title: Development of a multimodal research and treatment platform at Magdeburg University Hospital to characterise pathophysiological subgroups of patients with post-COVID syndrome and ME/CFS
summary:
The aim is to investigate the causes and disease-relevant mechanisms of the post-COVID condition and of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Both conditions can lead to persistent physical exhaustion, reduced exercise tolerance, difficulties concentrating (‘brain fog’) and other physical symptoms. The underlying disease mechanisms are not yet fully understood. 

The aim of this study is to gain a better understanding, through a combination of blood analyses, high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain, and tests to assess personality, mood, emotions and thinking (so-called psychometric and cognitive tests),
• what changes in the immune system
• what changes in blood flow and brain structure
• and what cognitive impairments (e.g. thought disorders)
occur in these conditions.

In the long term, the findings are intended to contribute to the development of new diagnostic approaches and potential therapeutic strategies.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients:
• Diagnosis of PCS or ME/CFS
• Suitable for an MRI scan
Study participants:
• No PCS or ME/CFS
• Suitable for an MRI scan
Exclusion criteria:
Patients:
• Neurological condition (other than PCS or ME/CFS) that explains the symptoms 
• Contraindication for an MRI scan 
Study participants:
• Neurological condition, known diagnosis of an autoimmune disease, a tumour or active or chronic infections
• Contraindication for an MRI scan
